source: hand-authored fixture for issue #223 — not shipped data
description: Shapes about WHICH MATCH lets a self-named allergy rule claim the identity chip's rank. (1) Opium's rule names the entry and carries a note, and Opium publishes a SECOND name ('papaveretum') that does not contain the rule's token — so a patient allergic to papaveretum and, separately, to Tiotropium gives the rule a mid-word containment match ('tiotropium' contains 'opium') while the allergen arm corroborates the substance from the other record. That is the only arrangement in which an accidental match and a genuine identity chip meet on one key. (2) Tiotropium is a real entry, so the accidental allergen resolves to something rather than to nothing. (3) Ibuprofen's rule names the entry and is exercised against an allergen recorded with a Romance inflection ('Ibuprofène'), which the drug-NAME rule's two-letter tail allowance reaches and a symmetric word boundary does not. (4) Ketoconazole (oral) and Levoketoconazole both publish 'ketoconazole' — the borrowed-alias shape of issue #224, authored so the two TIE on nameMatchStrength and the allergen arm therefore reaches both. (5) Levothyroxine publishes 'thyroxine' among its own names and rules on THAT name, so a patient whose allergy is recorded as 'Levothyroxine' matches the rule only mid-word while the ENTRY is exactly what the chart named — the shape that separates asking the question of the entry from asking it of the token, and the one a token-scoped rule demotes wrongly. No entry carries ATC codes, so no class comparison can chip and every count is the allergy arms' own.
